segment.description: Old Hickory Reservoir — a 22,500-acre USACE impoundment of the Cumberland River in northern middle Tennessee (dam completed 1954), catalog counties Davidson, Sumner, Wilson, Smith, and Trousdale. TWRA documents an entirely warmwater fishery (largemouth/smallmouth/spotted bass, crappie, striped/hybrid/white/yellow bass, walleye, sauger, paddlefish, catfish, sunfish) with no trout content anywhere on the page. This is a control-style water: no trout program has been found on any source checked.
segment.boundaries: Reservoir pool behind Old Hickory Dam (Cumberland River mile 216.2), east of Nashville; catalog counties Davidson, Sumner, Wilson, Smith, Trousdale.

coldSource.notes: TWRA: 'The US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) owns and operates Old Hickory Reservoir'; 'Old Hickory Reservoir is a 22,500-acre impoundment on the Cumberland River in northern middle Tennessee'; 'Dam completion occurred in 1954.' The reservoir is the impoundment itself, not a cold tailwater; no cold-release regime is documented.

holdover.detail: No trout fishery of any kind is documented: TWRA's reservoir page contains no mention of trout, the 2026 TWRA stocking schedule and owner workbook contain no Old Hickory trout rows, and no winter-program site on this impoundment exists (nearby Davidson winter sites — Shelby Bottoms, Cedar Hill Park Pond, Marrowbone Lake — are separate park/lake waters).

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented. TWRA's species list for the reservoir is entirely warmwater; the documented cold-season fishery associated with USACE dams on this river is sauger (a warmwater percids), not trout.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Warm mainstream Cumberland impoundment: TWRA's own reservoir page documents only warmwater species and no trout program exists for the lake on the 2026 stocking schedule or in the stocking workbook.
